en.title: Maximum and Minimum Median of a Fixed-Length Subsequence
en.description:
Choose any order-preserving subsequence of length k, sort it, and take its ⌈k/2⌉-th element as the median (for even lengths, the smaller middle value is taken, consistent with the source examples). Output the largest and the smallest median over all choices.

The standard I/O, examples, and judging were written independently by CSWork; conventions marked as this site's are not presented as original source constraints.
en.input: The first line contains n k (1≤k≤n≤100000), and the second line contains n values (0..10⁹).
en.output: Output the maximum median and the minimum median.
en.explanation: Example 1: the median is the smaller of the two chosen items; choosing [2,3] gives the maximum 2, and choosing [1,2] gives the minimum 1. Example 2: there is only 9, so both answers are 9. Example 3: the largest three items [3,4,5] have median 4, and the smallest three items [1,2,3] have median 2.
hints: Sort the array. The minimum median comes from the k smallest items, and the maximum median comes from the k largest items.
